title: Withdrawals failing
summary: Starting at 2026-10-15T17:48:12Z the payments-service began emitting dozens of errors indicating that calls to the external bank-rails dependency failed. The dependency is a hard HTTPS call with a 4 s timeout. No logs, metrics, or change‑history data are available for the window, so the exact trigger cannot be confirmed.

hypothesis.mechanism: An external outage or unannounced maintenance on bank-rails caused the HTTPS calls from payments-service to fail, which payments-service surfaces as “bank‑rails call returned an error”.
predictions: Bank‑rails status page or support shows an incident around 17:45‑18:00.
When metrics recover, bank‑rails error‑rate and latency series will show a spike at the same time.

hypothesis.mechanism: A recent code deploy introduced a bug in handling bank‑rails responses, causing every call to be treated as an error starting at 17:48.
predictions: A deploy record for payments-service will appear at ~17:40‑17:48 once change history is available.
Rolling back the deploy would immediately stop the errors.

hypothesis.mechanism: A network, DNS, or TLS/certificate problem between payments-service and bank-rails caused the HTTPS calls to fail (handshake error, timeout, cert validation failure).
predictions: Certificate transparency logs or internal cert‑monitoring will show a cert expiry/rotation near 17:45.
Network flow logs will show increased TCP resets or TLS alerts for the payments‑service → bank‑rails path.

hypothesis.mechanism: A configuration change reduced the HTTP client timeout or tightened a circuit‑breaker threshold, so normal bank‑rails latency now exceeds the limit and is logged as an error.
predictions: Config audit will reveal a timeout or breaker setting changed at ~17:40‑17:48.
Reverting the config change will restore success rate without a code rollback.

facts.statement: payments-service logged 44 ERROR lines “withdrawal <id> failed: bank-rails call returned an error” from 17:48:12Z to 17:59:37Z.
Dependency graph shows a hard HTTPS dependency payments-service → bank-rails with a 4000 ms timeout.

assumptions.statement: The error text “bank‑rails call returned an error” is emitted only when the downstream HTTP call fails (non‑2xx, timeout, TLS error, etc.).
assumptions.reason: Observed error pattern matches typical client‑side HTTP failure logging.

assumptions.statement: A deploy to payments-service could have been rolled out a few minutes before 17:48 but is invisible because the change‑history API is down.
assumptions.reason: No change data available for the window; deploy timing is a common cause of sudden error spikes.

assumptions.statement: No other service (e.g., edge‑gateway) shows errors, suggesting the problem is confined to the payments‑service → bank‑rails link.
assumptions.reason: Only payments‑service logs contain the failure pattern.

assumptions.statement: A config change (e.g., lowered timeout or circuit‑breaker threshold) could have been applied just before 17:48 but is not captured.
assumptions.reason: Hard dependency with a 4 s timeout; tightening it would produce the same symptom.

actions.description: Contact bank‑rails vendor (status page, support) to confirm any outage or maintenance around 17:45‑18:00.
actions.rationale: Directly tests the most likely hypothesis (H1) that the external dependency degraded.

actions.description: Retrieve payments-service metrics (error rate, latency, saturation) once the metrics backend recovers and correlate with the 17:48 error spike.
actions.rationale: Quantifies impact and confirms whether the error rate matches log volume.

actions.description: Re‑run get_change_history (or query CI/CD) for payments-service and bank-rails to locate any deploy, config, feature‑flag, secret rotation, or infra work at ~17:40‑17:50.
actions.rationale: Needed to validate or discard hypotheses H2, H4 (code regression or config change).

actions.description: Request detailed error codes / logs from bank‑rails (HTTP status, TLS alerts) for the failing calls.
actions.rationale: Determines exact failure mode (timeout, cert error, rate‑limit) to discriminate H1 vs H3.

actions.description: Add a circuit‑breaker / fallback for the bank‑rails call in payments-service and improve alerting on hard‑dependency error rates.
actions.rationale: Reduces blast radius for future provider issues regardless of root cause.

actions.description: Verify certificate expiry and TLS configuration for the payments‑service → bank‑rails connection; automate renewal monitoring.
Extend log retention to cover at least 2 hours before any alert so early warning patterns are not lost.
actions.rationale: Addresses gap F7 and improves future investigations.

open_questions: Did bank‑rails publish a maintenance window or experience an unplanned outage at ~17:45?
Was there a payments-service deploy or config push between 17:30‑17:48 that is invisible to the change‑history API?
What exact HTTP status or TLS error did the bank‑rails call return? (requires provider logs.)
Why are the metrics and change‑history back‑ends currently down—are they related to the same incident?
Are any upstream services (e.g., edge‑gateway) seeing elevated 5xx that would indicate a broader platform issue?
